''10. In earth.'') {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Chri{{ls}}t remitteth {{ls}}innes by the Prie{{ls}}ts mini{{ls}}terie.}}This power that the Sonne of man hath to remitte {{ls}}innes in earth, was neuer taken from him, but dureth {{ls}}till in his Sacraments, and mini{{ls}}ters, by whom he remitteth {{ls}}innes in the Church, and not in heauen only. {{c|''The blind Phari{{ls}}ees {{ls}}eeking his death for doing good vpon the Sabboths, he meekely goeth out of the vvay: vvhere the people that flocke vnto him, and his Miracles, are innumerable. 13 Yea to his Tvvelue al{{ls}}o (hauing neede of moe vvorkmen) he geueth povver to vvorke Miracles. 20 He {{ls}}o occupieth him {{ls}}elf for {{ls}}oules, that his kinne thinke him madde. 22 The Scribes of Hieru{{ls}}alem come {{ls}}o farre, and yet haue nothing but ab{{ls}}urdly to bla{{ls}}peme his ca{{ls}}ting out of Diuels, to their ovvne damnation. 31 That the Ievves {{ls}}hould not (after their maner) thinke it ynough, that he is of their bloud, he telleth that {{ls}}uch rather are deere to him, as keepe Gods commaundements.''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=3|verse=1}}}}{{sc|Nd}} he entred againe into the Synagogue, and there vvas a man there that had a vvithered hand.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 12, 9. Lu. 6, 6.''}} {{verse|chapter=3|verse=2}}† And they vvatched him vvhether he vvould cure on the Sabboths: that they might accu{{ls}}e him. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=3}}† And he {{ls}}aith to the man that had the vvithered hand, Ri{{ls}}e vp into the middes. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=4}}† And he {{ls}}aith to them, Is it lavvful on the Sabboths to doe vvel or il? to {{ls}}aue a {{ls}}oule, or to de{{ls}}troy? but they held their peace. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=5}}† And looking round about vpon them vvith anger, being {{ls}}orovvful for the blindenes of their hart, he {{ls}}aith to the man, Stretch forth thy hand.
